page.title: The stream at about 60 metres
page.description: The stream at about 60 metres. Recorded at about 60 m in the Glenabo catchment, Fermoy, Co. Cork.

hero.title: The stream at about 60 metres.
hero.alt: A shallow stony stream running through woodland with exposed gravel bars

blocks.text:
You are standing about forty metres above the point where this water meets the *Munster Blackwater*, and six hundred and fifty metres from it. Everything that falls on about 320 hectares upstream of here passes this spot.

Look at the bed. The stones are angular and the gravel bars are loose. Loose sediment on a stream bed is one of the things that decides whether it can hold fish, because eggs laid in gravel need clean water moving through them.

blocks.heading: The name of this glen
blocks.text: An account written down at Adair school in the 1930s explains how Glenabo got its name. It names the glen, not this particular spot.
